title: Legal comms & pricing alignment workshop
summary: Workshop to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing approval path and technical risk mitigation (SSO/KMS/data residency). Redwood AE/SE explained hosting vs Dedicated tradeoffs; customer raised strict data residency and audit log requirements. Agreed to run a Proof-of-Concept for a scoped workload and deliver security package + pricing worksheet by next week.
topics: KMS/SSO integration and key management options
Pricing approval path and finance sign-off
action_items: Samir Patel - Send redlined MSA excerpt and DPA summary highlighting acceptable clauses - Due 2027-09-20
Maya Chen - Prepare pilot runbook and target latency/cost spreadsheet for scoped workload - Due 2027-09-21
Elliot Rivers - Share SOC2 + pen-test summary and audit log retention options - Due 2027-09-19
Priya Raman - Provide list of non-negotiable DPA items and desired data residency jurisdictions - Due 2027-09-18
next_steps: Redwood to provide security package (SOC2, pen-test, KMS integration doc) via shared drive
Redwood to propose pilot SOW and indicative pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted lanes
Customer legal to mark DPA/MAA exceptions and meet again after internal review
Schedule pilot kickoff session week of 2027-09-27
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, Maya Chen, Elliot Rivers (Redwood); Liza Gomez, Derek Wu, Priya Raman, Owen Hart (Horizon)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I know this is the legal and procurement alignment workshop, so we'll try to be concise. agenda is MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing path and a pilot ask.
[00:20] Liza: great, thanks Samir. quick context, we have a three week window for vendor recommend to procurement committee, finance wants ballpark numbers, legal is looking for DPA not to include broad subprocessor clauses.
[00:35] Priya: yes, prioritize data residency - anything touching PHI has to sit in EU and US-east only, and we need clear audit logs for six years.
[00:50] Maya: understood. from a tech perspective our Private and Dedicated deploys can be pinned to region, and we have audit log retention options, though there are some tradeoffs for latency and cost with longer retention.
[01:10] Derek: can you spell out KMS options? on-prem HSM vs cloud KMS, and who holds keys?
[01:25] Samir: yes, we support customer-managed keys in both Dedicated and Redwood Private flows. small caveat, for hosted we offer CMEK via major cloud providers, for Private we can do HSM or vault integrations, there might be additional setup time and fee.
[01:45] Owen: and what about SSO? we need SAML+SCIM provisioning.
[01:50] Elliot: we do SSO SAML and SCIM, role mappings and RBAC are supported in the console, we can show mapping examples in the pilot. sometimes the SCIM mapping needs a little hand-holding for groups.
[02:10] Priya: on the MSA, our counsel flagged the indemnity and liability caps — we usually push for a higher cap on data incidents and narrower carveouts.
[02:25] Samir: understood, in past we've seen a pattern: customers want higher cap, vendors push for capped liability. we can escalate required MSA clauses to legal ops; I'll mark which clauses are more flexible.
[02:45] Liza: finance needs a pricing path: what is the delta between hosted and dedicated, and is there a commit model?
[02:55] Samir: yes, hosted is pay-as-you-go, lower up-front friction; Dedicated has reserved capacity model with monthly commit and lower per-token cost. we'll send a sample worksheet showing TCO for expected qps.
[03:20] Derek: any quick numbers for a 50qps baseline? latency target 95th percentile <120ms per token for inference.
[03:35] Maya: rough thumb: Hosted for that workload would be about 1.4x the per-token cost vs a mid-sized Dedicated pool. latency depends on model shape and batch policy; with batching and caching we can meet 95p 120ms for short prompts, long-context might spike.
[04:00] Priya: on the DPA, we need subprocessor lists and a mechanism to approve subprocessor changes. can you commit to notice period?
[04:15] Samir: yes we typically provide a subprocessor list and 30 days' notice for changes, exceptions can be discussed.
[04:30] Owen: do you offer any SLA credits tied to SLOs? procurement usually wants a formal SLA with credits.
[04:40] Elliot: yes, for Dedicated we offer SLA with uptime targets and credits; Hosted has best-effort with published perf profiles and availability tiers. we'll attach the SLA draft.
[04:55] Liza: legal will look for a remedy matrix.
[05:00] Priya: also we have encryption-at-rest requirements and want to ensure keys are never exfiltrated. what's your operational access model?
[05:12] Maya: operationally we have role-based access, KMS audit logs, and we can stop support staff from accessing customer keys where CMEK is used. for Private deployments customers retain control.
[05:30] Derek: does Redwood keep logs of raw prompts? retention policy?
[05:40] Samir: default is short retention for hosted telemetry, customers on Dedicated/Private control retention. we'll provide a table with defaults and configurable knobs.
[06:05] Liza: ok, high level seems promising. the tricky bits are DPA carveouts and the liability cap, plus finance needs the delta in committed costs.
[06:20] Samir: proposal: we run a pilot on a non-PHI dataset scoped to a single EU region to demonstrate perf and audit exports. that gives legal and security the artifacts they need.
[06:35] Priya: pilot is fine as long as we capture logs and you guarantee deletion process post-pilot.
[06:45] Elliot: yes we can provide a runbook and post-pilot sanitization cert.
[07:00] Owen: timeline: if pilot kicks off week of 9/27, we can present to finance 10/11.
[07:10] Samir: that aligns with our SOW cadence. we'll prepare an SOW for pilot and indicative pricing.
[10:05] [discussion drift: details on SOW line items and what 'scoped workload' means, slightly fuzzy transcription]
[12:20] Derek: technical ask: can you support customer KMS but have Redwood manage rotation?
[12:35] Maya: rotation can be automated by customer KMS — Redwood won't hold plaintext keys; rotations are propagated via API. we'll include the integration diagram.
[15:00] Priya: on DPA exceptions, our legal says no automatic data transfer to outside designated regions even for failover unless explicitly approved.
[15:20] Samir: we can map failover policies to approval flows; automatic global failover can be disabled for the account.
[18:30] Liza: about subprocessor transparency, what does the notice look like? email? portal?
[18:40] Elliot: portal notice plus email to designated legal contacts. we can add webhook feed if you want automated alerts.
[21:50] Owen: pricing question, do you support step-down pricing after certain volume thresholds?
[22:05] Samir: yes Tiered pricing is common; committed volume discounts can be layered — we'll show examples.
[25:00] [brief silence and cross-talk while screensharing pricing worksheet]
[28:10] Priya: liability cap language example: 1M for data incidents is low for us; can you accept a higher cap tied to revenue?
[28:35] Samir: we can propose a middle-ground escalation: higher cap for Dedicated enterprise customers subject to added insurance endorsements. I'll flag that to contracts.
[30:00] Liza: what about audit rights? we need to know if we can run independent audits.
[30:12] Elliot: we offer audit support and provide SOC2 reports; independent audits are negotiable and often handled as scoped engagements.
[33:00] Priya: retention again, six years is long. can you support archival export for long-term retention rather than keeping live logs?
[33:15] Maya: yes archiving to customer storage is possible; we can export logs to S3/GCS with lifecycle policies.
[36:20] Owen: who signs the order form? procurement needs an approved signature line and finance contact.
[36:32] Samir: Samir Patel, AE will be main contact; we'll provide PO wiring info in the proposal.
[40:00] [group summarizes ask items and timelines]
[42:50] Liza: if you can get us the security pack and a redline example within the week, we'll try to push to committee by 10/04.
[43:05] Samir: yes, we'll aim for that.
[46:00] Priya: one more question: are there any export controls or encryption restrictions we should be aware of?
[46:12] Elliot: we support customer-side encryption and can segregate compute by region; nothing special but we'll note any regulatory caveats per region.
[48:30] Derek: can you also include a brief on incident response SLAs and escalation chain?
[48:40] Elliot: we'll include incident response times and on-call escalation matrix in the SLA draft.
[50:10] Samir: ok let's recap next steps, action owners and dates. thanks everyone for pragmatic discussion.
[50:25] Liza: thanks all, we'll review docs and Priya will post her DPA items.
[51:00] Priya: thanks, I'll push our exceptions by end of Friday.
[51:10] Samir: perfect. Samir signing off.
[51:20] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional dropouts during screen share; product names sometimes mis-typed (Redwood Private transcribed as 'Redwood private/privat'). Some timestamps approximate.
